newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Diesel sold to China at low $216/T for end-Jan.
newsitem.headline: Diesel sold to China at low $216/T for end-Jan.

text.p: China's state-owned Sinochem late last week bought 30,000 tonnes of gas oil (diesel) at $216 per tonne for end-January delivery, cost-and-freight (c-and-f) southern China basis, traders said on Monday.

A trading source said the price was a hefty $40 below the last deal sold to China about two weeks ago. Gas oil offered to China in December reached a peak of $260-$263, c-and-f for January arrival cargoes.
The source said the low price sold recently could spell "trouble for endusers" who have bought at record high prices earlier and might cause some of them to default.
Traders said a number of sellers might have already been caught by buyers who refused to take delivery of cargoes that they had already purchased.

Chinese source said a Singapore trader has about 150,000 tonnes floating in tankers off China because some buyers have defaulted. Traders said a major and two other trading firms might have also suffered the same fate.

One source said in addition to the drastic drop in prices, sellers also have to contend with a deadline in delivery the cargoes as Chinese port workers take their Lunar New Year leave from January 25 for about two-weeks to return to their home provinces.
As a result, China is not in the market to buy early February cargoes and is now looking for cargoes for second-half February delivery.
Gas oil prices in Singapore dropped by about $4.00 a barrel over the past week to the current $27.50-$28.00 a barrel, free-on-board (fob) Singapore basis, primarily due to China's absence.
Prices peaked at $34.45 a barrel in early December when China emerged to buy large volumes to cover acute shortages.

Traders said regional demand was not expected to pick up in the near term despite emerging demand from Indonesia for February and market expectations that India might buy about the same volume for March delivery as they did in February which was 855,000 tonnes.
